recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source change is needed for FHIR-14408 unless a future work group decision changes the RequestOrchestration action type model; the related PlanDefinition issue FHIR-14407 should remain a separate decision.
issue_request: FHIR-14408 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 change request to change RequestGroup.action.type from Coding to CodeableConcept because extensible bindings should be modeled on CodeableConcept.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN 13266, represented in git by b17b8633b3a52671552e06efc12ee110e5a577ab, whose message cites GF#14408 and whose RequestGroup spreadsheet diff changes RequestGroup.action.type from Coding to CodeableConcept.
additional_context: RequestGroup was later renamed to RequestOrchestration. The active fhir.ini resource entry is requestorchestration=RequestOrchestration, the legacy migration map records RequestGroup=@RequestOrchestration, and commit 46bea37a00e63d1ace04a5f322614c6d0815f500 performed that rename. A 2016 terminology Zulip thread provides background supporting the CodeableConcept rationale, while targeted direct FHIR-14408 Zulip and Confluence searches found no later conflicting record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the build-scope StructureDefinition already defines RequestOrchestration.action.type as CodeableConcept with extensible ActionType binding to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/action-type.

related_jiras.note: The same 2018 implementation commit also changed PlanDefinition.action.type, but that separate artifact was outside this seed decision.
The later RequestGroup-to-RequestOrchestration rename explains why the current source path and element name differ from the STU3 Jira wording.

evidence_items.summary: RequestOrchestration.action.type is defined as CodeableConcept with extensible ActionType binding to terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/action-type.
evidence_items.learned: The current authoritative source already implements the FHIR-14408 datatype change.
